Created by the writer and artist Lee Sharks', a five-document 'hand' — Whose Face Is on the Twenty? (thumb), The Lizard People Were Right (index), All the Spoils of Babylon (middle), The Inauguration of Memography (ring), the Charter (pinky) — and the title from a 'recurring absurdist motif… using prize money to replace friends and family with "moving statues made of rubies"'. Attested: the hand and its fingers (#505: 'Thumb: "Whose Face Is on the Twenty?"', the index finger that 'points at the mechanism'); the motif is Pearl's author note ('He has used MacArthur money to replace his friends and family with moving statues made of rubies'). The Charter (#505) and Whose Face (#502) are Rex Fraction's; the Lizard People (#508) is Lee Sharks's; 'Created by… Lee Sharks' gives the room to the orthonym. Against 13 June (signed in): then 'a conceptual art project and narrative piece… a theoretical and curatorial framework rather than a physical mint', sourced to Frieze and others, 'Crimson Hexagon' for 'Crimson Hexagonal'; now the five-document hand, the Pearl bio and an author, from Medium, crimsonhexagonal.org and this registry's June page.
